name: Chicken Kolhapuri

fit.note: 604 cal sits at the top edge of the 400-650 band and 19g carbs is safely mid-band; published numbers clear all conditions. Candidate's own caveat is that a label-accurate recompute (3 tbsp oil over 3 servings) could brush the 650 ceiling, but the published figure is FIT.

evidence: Not a duplicate: the nearest catalog chicken curries are structurally different dinners. kadai-chicken-karahi (bell pepper + tomato + cream, no coconut/poppy/sesame) and chicken-jalfrezi (bell-pepper stir-fry) lack the signature roasted Kolhapuri masala; chicken-madras-curry is coconut-milk based and south-indian-chettinad-pepper-chicken-bowls is a Tamil pepper-forward prep. Kolhapuri's defining roasted dry-coconut/white-poppy/sesame/whole-spice masala and fiery Maharashtrian profile make it a distinct regional dish, and no Kolhapuri/Maharashtrian entry exists in the catalog digest (544 recipes) or accepted-slugs.
cuisine_spread_value: high - adds a Maharashtrian entry the catalog lacks; the Indian-chicken-curry cluster is already dense (madras, jalfrezi, rogan-josh, vindaloo, kadai/karahi, chettinad, tikka-masala variants, trinidadian) so this widens region within an existing cuisine rather than a new cuisine.
cross_protein_collision_watch: Kolhapuri masala is applied to mutton/lamb as often as chicken in Maharashtrian cooking - a lamb/mutton 'Kolhapuri' or 'Maharashtrian [protein] curry' in the beef/lamb pool would be the same dish under a different protein. Decider should also watch for a goat/mutton kadai or generic 'spicy Indian [protein] curry' twin.
borderline_note: Adjacent-but-distinct to kadai-chicken-karahi and chettinad within a dense Indian-curry cluster; flagged for decider visibility, not a dupe.
